LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 1.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND LISTENING COMPREHENSION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: CHILD LABOUR Suggested Vocabulary an orphanage, orphan, domestic, servant, work,
Topic 1.1: Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension, part of CHILD LABOUR Suggested Vocabulary an orphanage, orphan, domestic, servant, work, in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade six ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why should you listen keenly? 2. What is the importance of proper pronunciation of words?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1.  Listen to an oral narrative from a digital device or a text read by the teacher,  Listen for specific information such as sounds: /ɪə/ as in tears, appear, rear, clear and severe from a text,  Listen for the main idea from a text, practise saying words with the sound /ɪə/, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/point/sign/write) to express their views 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1.  Listen to an oral narrative from a digital device or a text read by the teacher,  Listen for specific information such as sounds: /ɪə/ as in tears, appear, rear, clear and severe from a text,  Listen for the main idea from a text, practise saying words with the sound /ɪə/, Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication-AAC (residual speech/ digital devices with text-to- speech application/point/sign/write) to express their views 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Listening Comprehension together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital Literacy: The learner’s interaction with technology is enhanced as they manipulate digital devices when listening to an

oral narrative.

Learning to Learn: The learner’s ability to grasp concepts is cultivated as they carry out pronunciation an retelling of stories with

peers.

4

Responsibility: The learner shows accountability when listening to an oral narrative from a digital device.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:

Child Rights: The learner’s knowledge on the rights of children is enhanced as they listen and respond to texts on Child Labour.

Link to other Subjects

The learner uses proper pronunciation and acquires vocabulary learnt on the theme of Child Labour to learn a similar concept in

Kiswahili and other Languages.
